propositions.text: The appellant is a citizen of Lebanon.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (the appellant) is a citizen of Lebanon.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellant is a citizen of Lebanon.

propositions.text: The appellant fears persecution by Hizballah in Lebanon due to opposition to their land acquisition.
propositions.quote: The appellant fears persecution by members of the Hizballah party in Lebanon because he opposed their acquisition of land and property in his region.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellant fears persecution by Hizballah for opposing their land acquisition.

propositions.text: The RPD found the appellant not credible due to failure to mention threats, inconsistency about the persecutor, and no protective measures taken.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) found that the appellant was not credible because of his failure to mention threatening telephone calls, because of an inconsistency in the profile of the agent of persecution, and because of his failure to take any protective measures from the time he received the threats until he left Lebanon.

propositions.text: The RPD concluded an internal flight alternative was available in Lebanon.
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that an internal flight alternative (IFA) was available to him in Lebanon.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the appellant not credible and concluded an internal flight alternative was available.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD erred in concluding Hizballah would not pursue him because they did not target him or his family.
propositions.quote: The appellant argues that the RPD erred in basing its conclusion that Hizballah would not pursue him on the fact that they did not target him while he was still in Lebanon and have not attacked his family, who have remained in the village since his departure.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD erred in concluding an internal flight alternative was available in another city in Lebanon.
propositions.quote: He further argues that the RPD erred in concluding that an IFA was available to him in another city in Lebanon.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred on Hizballah's pursuit and availability of internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: The determinative issue is whether the RPD erred in its analysis of the appellant's credibility.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) considers that the determinative issue is whether or not the RPD erred in its analysis of the appellant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD identifies the key issue as whether the RPD erred in analyzing the appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed; the RPD was correct that the appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal. The RPD was correct in determining that the appellant is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD dismisses the appeal, agreeing with the RPD's determination that the appellant is not a refugee or protected person.

propositions.text: The RAD's role is to examine all evidence and determine if the RPD's decision is correct.
propositions.quote: My role is to examine all of the evidence and to determine whether the RPD's decision is correct.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD states its role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD's decision is correct.

propositions.text: The appellant was invited to submit documents or observations about resumption of deadlines due to COVID-19 but submitted none.
propositions.quote: On June 15, 2020, the appellant received a notice concerning the status of his appeal inviting him to submit to the RAD any documents or observations pertaining to the resumption of deadlines in light of the COVID-19 pandemic. Any such documents or observations were to be provided within 30 days following the date on which he received the notice. As of the date of this decision, the appellant has submitted no observations or new evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the appellant was invited to submit COVID-19 related documents but submitted none.

propositions.text: Appellant's sworn facts are presumed true unless valid reason to doubt arises on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: The appellant has sworn that the facts on the record are complete, true and correct. His allegations are therefore presumed to be true, unless a valid reason to doubt their truthfulness arises in the course of assessing the evidence on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: The appellant's testimony is not credible due to failure to mention telephone death threats from Hizballah.
propositions.quote: For the reasons that follow, the appellant's testimony is not credible. The appellant, XXXX XXXX, failed to mention the telephone death threats from Hizballah

paragraphs.summary: The court states sworn facts are presumed true unless doubted; here, the appellant's testimony is not credible due to omission of death threats.

propositions.text: The RPD noted the appellant failed to mention telephone threats in his Basis of Claim Form and drew a negative credibility inference.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted a significant omission in the appellant's Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form), in that he failed to mention the telephone threats he referred to during the hearing. The RPD drew a negative credibility inference from this omission.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the appellant's failure to mention telephone threats in his claim form undermined his credibility.

propositions.text: The appellant said he did not remember the threats until the hearing.
propositions.quote: The appellant acknowledged that he did not mention these threats in his BOC Form, stating that he had not remembered them until the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant says he forgot to mention the threats until the hearing.

propositions.text: The RPD's conclusion that the appellant's failure to mention threats undermines credibility is correct.
propositions.quote: The RPD's conclusion is correct. The appellant did not mention the telephone threats in his BOC Form, and this undermines his credibility.

propositions.text: The appellant devoted few lines to threats in his BOC Form, only one paragraph describing threats from Hizballah.
propositions.quote: In his BOC Form, the appellant devoted 23 lines to describing his life before the events in question, 20 lines to describing the steps he took to come to Canada, and only 12 lines to describing the events surrounding the threats from Hizballah. All of the appellant's allegations concerning these threats are contained in a single paragraph: "In XXXX 2018, when Hezbollah members found out about my involvement against them they threatened me, my family and my children. They told me exactly 'if you oppose our activity again, we will give you a lesson and we are capable to get you even if you were underground'."

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees the appellant's failure to mention threats in detail undermines credibility, noting the brief description in his claim form.

propositions.text: It is unlikely the appellant forgot to mention the threats as they are central to his claim and instructions were clear.
propositions.quote: It is unlikely that he would forget to mention these threatening calls if he had in fact received them, since he only needed to describe three or four telephone threats and one face-to-face threat.

propositions.text: BOC Form instructions require all important information including events, dates and places to be provided.
propositions.quote: The instructions at question 2(a) of the BOC Form are clear: the appellant was to provide all information that is important to establishing his allegations, including the events, dates and places.

propositions.text: The appellant was likely aware of instructions because a lawyer helped complete the form.
propositions.quote: On a balance of probabilities, the appellant was aware of these instructions, because a lawyer helped him complete the claim form.

propositions.text: The appellant's omission of important threats central to his claim undermines his credibility.
propositions.quote: The appellant failed to mention these important threats in his form; these threats are central to his claim for refugee protection, and this omission undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant likely knew instructions but omitted central threats, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: The RPD believed the appellant would have taken protective measures if his life had been threatened since July 2018.
propositions.quote: The RPD was of the opinion that if the appellant's life had been threatened by Hizballah since July 2018, he would have taken other measures to try to protect himself and his family.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the appellant would have taken protective measures if truly threatened since July 2018.

propositions.text: The appellant said he had nowhere to go and stayed home at night, going out little during the day to avoid Hizballah.
propositions.quote: The appellant alleged that he had nowhere to go and that Hizballah members did not come to his house because he stayed home at night and went out as little as possible during the day.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant says he stayed home mostly and had nowhere to go to avoid Hizballah.

propositions.text: The appellant's behaviour of staying home but going out occasionally undermines credibility given the threat from Hizballah.
propositions.quote: The RPD's conclusion is correct. The appellant's credibility is undermined by his behaviour in remaining at home for five months without taking any precautions other than avoiding going out during the day, even though a dangerous organization wanted to kill him.

propositions.text: The appellant stayed home for about five months after the death threat before leaving Lebanon.
propositions.quote: The death threat that prompted him to leave was allegedly made in XXXX 2018, and he left his country on XXXX XXXX, 2019. Thus, he stayed at his home for approximately five months.

propositions.text: A person fearing for life from a dangerous group would go into hiding or avoid going out entirely, unlike the appellant's behaviour.
propositions.quote: On a balance of probabilities, when a person's life is threatened by a group as dangerous as Hizballah, that person will go into hiding to protect their life. At a minimum, if they remain in their own home, they will not go out at all and will pretend they are not there in order to avoid an attack by the agents of persecution.

propositions.text: The appellant's decision to remain home and go out occasionally is inconsistent with fearing for life, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: The appellant's decision to remain in his own home, to wait until he had the money he needed to leave, and to even go out on a few occasions is not the behaviour of a person who fears for their life. I draw a negative credibility inference from this behaviour.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant's behaviour of occasionally going out undermines credibility given the serious threat.

propositions.text: The RPD concluded Hizballah was not interested in the appellant as they made no effort to find him or pressure his family.
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that Hizballah was not interested in the appellant because they put no effort into looking for him and have not pressured his family since he left.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found Hizballah showed no interest in the appellant or his family after he left.

propositions.text: The appellant argues Hizballah does not target families and that lack of attack before departure does not mean no future attack.
propositions.quote: The appellant argues that it is not customary for Hizballah members to go after their targets' wives and children and that he would not have left the country if his family had been in danger. He argues that the fact that Hizballah did not attack him between XXXX 2018 and XXXX 2019 does not mean they will not attack him once they realize that the resistance he formed with his neighbours is alive and well and that it is stronger than Hizballah thought it was.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues Hizballah does not attack families and lack of prior attack does not preclude future attack.

propositions.text: Hizballah did not attack the appellant during five months he was accessible, showing lack of interest.
propositions.quote: Hizballah did not attack the appellant while he was at home in Lebanon for five months before his departure.

propositions.text: Appellant went out during the day a few times and nothing happened.
propositions.quote: He not only stayed in his own home, but also went out during the day on a few occasions, and nothing happened to him.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows Hizballah can find anyone in Lebanon when looking for them.
propositions.quote: Yet according to the documentary evidence, when Hizballah is looking for someone, even the Lebanese authorities are unable to protect that person.

propositions.text: Everyone knew where the appellant lived, making him easy to find.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the appellant explained at the hearing that everyone knew where he lived.

propositions.text: The lack of attack despite accessibility confirms Hizballah has no interest in the appellant and unlikely to attack if he returns.
propositions.quote: The fact that Hizballah did not attack him during the five months when he was easily accessible confirms that they have no interest in him and makes it unlikely that they would attack him if he returned to Lebanon.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence indicates Hizballah neutralizes existential threats with no compromise.
propositions.quote: This lack of interest is confirmed by the documentary evidence indicating that anyone who is considered to pose an existential or imminent threat to Hizballah's security is subject to close monitoring and neutralization; there is no compromise.

propositions.text: If appellant was a person of interest, Hizballah would have attacked before he left, which they did not.
propositions.quote: If the appellant was a person of interest to Hizballah, they would have attacked him before he left, which they did not do.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Hizballah did not attack the appellant despite opportunity, confirming lack of interest and undermining claim.

propositions.text: The appellant argues Hizballah does not attack families and he would not have left if family was in danger.
propositions.quote: The appellant argues that Hizballah does not attack the families of its enemies. The documentary evidence does not support this assertion. The appellant further argues that he would not have left his country if he had believed his family was in danger.

propositions.text: The appellant contradicts himself by alleging Hizballah would not attack family but fearing for their lives, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: However, he states in his appeal memorandum that he [translation] "feared for his life and the lives of his wife and children," as he also wrote in his BOC Form. The appellant is contradicting himself. He is alleging both that Hizballah would not attack his family because that is not their practice and also that he feared for the lives of his family members. This undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues Hizballah does not attack families, but contradicts himself fearing for their lives, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: Hizballah would target him because he opposed land sales to them in his village
propositions.quote: The appellant argues that Hizballah would be motivated to target him if he returned to the country because he was the instigator of the front formed in his village to oppose the sale of land to the organization

propositions.text: Hizballah's failure to attack him in 2018-2019 does not mean they won't if he returns
propositions.quote: he further argues that the fact that Hizballah did not attack him in 2018-2019 does not mean they will not do so if he returns to Lebanon

propositions.text: This is speculation and not supported by facts; Hizballah did not attack him, his family, or neighbours since he left
propositions.quote: This is speculation and is not supported by the facts. Hizballah did not attack him and have not attacked his family since he left, nor have they attacked the appellant's neighbours who were also part of the group that opposed the land sales

propositions.text: His wife's family who refused to sell land to Hizballah have not been bothered since his departure
propositions.quote: His wife's family members, who own land and refused to sell to Hizballah, have also not been bothered since his departure

propositions.text: Two family members left the country but no evidence they left due to threats
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the appellant explained that two of them have left the country, but nothing in the evidence suggests that they left because of any threats made against them

propositions.text: Three or four others stayed but no evidence Hizballah attacked them
propositions.quote: The appellant also stated that three or four other people had stayed, but he did not testify or establish that Hizballah has attacked them either

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues Hizballah would target him if he returns; the court finds no attacks or threats against him or family since he left.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence does not support appellant's hypothesis about Hizballah's land purchases
propositions.quote: the documentary evidence does not support the appellant's hypothesis

propositions.text: Hizballah buys land from Christians, not Sunni Muslims like appellant and his community
propositions.quote: they buy land from Christians, not from Sunni Muslims like the appellant and his community

propositions.text: Land is acquired to be sold to Muslims, not for offices or a party centre as appellant claims
propositions.quote: land is acquired so that it can be sold to Muslims, not so that it can be used for offices and a centre for the party, as the appellant states in his account

propositions.text: Some municipalities oppose such land transactions, but the appellant's village city hall did nothing
propositions.quote: a number of municipalities oppose this type of transaction, although the city hall in the appellant's village chose to do nothing

paragraphs.summary: The court finds documentary evidence contradicts appellant's claims about Hizballah's land purchases and intentions.

propositions.text: No interest shown by Hizballah in attacking appellant or family undermines his credibility
propositions.quote: The fact that Hizballah has shown no interest in attacking the appellant either directly or indirectly, through his family, and that the documentary evidence does not support the appellant's version of the facts undermines his credibility

propositions.text: Appellant has not credibly established on balance of probabilities that Hizballah threatens his life
propositions.quote: The appellant has not credibly established, on a balance of probabilities, that Hizballah has any interest in him and is threatening his life

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's credibility undermined and he has not proven Hizballah threatens his life.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's credibility fatally undermined on key refugee claim elements
propositions.quote: The points noted by the RPD (and the RAD) provide sufficient grounds to conclude that the appellant's credibility has been fatally undermined with respect to the key elements of his refugee protection claim

propositions.text: Appellant failed to mention telephone threats in BOC Form
propositions.quote: he failed to mention a key element of his claim in his BOC Form (the telephone threats)

propositions.text: Appellant's behaviour inconsistent with fear or risk of harm during five months at home with family
propositions.quote: his behaviour was inconsistent with a fear or risk of harm during the five months he remained in his own home with his family

propositions.text: Appellant failed to establish Hizballah has any interest in him
propositions.quote: he failed to establish that Hizballah has any interest in him

propositions.text: RPD made no errors in these findings
propositions.quote: The RPD made no errors

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's credibility fatally undermined; the court finds no errors in that conclusion.

propositions.text: Appellant has not credibly established serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned
propositions.quote: The appellant has not credibly established that, should he return to Lebanon, he would face a serious possibility of persecution by members of Hizballah, or that he would face a danger of torture, a risk to his life, or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes appellant has not proven serious risk of persecution or harm if returned to Lebanon.

propositions.text: No need to address appellant's arguments on internal flight alternative given conclusion
propositions.quote: it is not necessary for me to respond to the appellant's arguments concerning the RPD's conclusion on the internal flight alternative in Lebanon

paragraphs.summary: The court declines to address internal flight alternative arguments due to prior conclusion.

propositions.text: Appeal dismissed; RPD's determination that appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection is confirmed
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal and confirm the RPD's determination that the appellant, XXXX XXXX, is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD's decision denying refugee protection.
